agree.reason: The GM gets a direct answer on the renovation, the budget gap and the outside candidate, and 7 weeks already doing the job is hard to wave away, though the case against bigger-hotel experience rests mostly on knowing this building.

honest.reason: It drops the 'main reason' claim, says the renovation helped, and 'almost half' (0.3 of 0.7) is accurate; 'each month' for a 7-week stretch is only a slight stretch.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the share of the score gain before the renovation and the cut in training time, but misses that the score rose about twice as fast per month before the renovation (0.3 in 5 months vs 0.4 in 13), and leaves turnover as raw counts when it could say it fell from 64% to 36%.

right_comparison.reason: It splits the score gain into before and after the renovation and compares turnover before and after her promotion, and it describes the outside candidate fairly, though the claim that an outside hire would lose months learning the hotel is asserted, not shown.

qualification.reason: The budget fix gives checkable commitments (finance course within 3 months, weekly sessions with a named controller), but there's no measurable target and nothing said about what happens if they're missed.

objections.reason: It takes on the GM's three likely objections (renovation, no budget experience, outside candidate's experience) head-on and doesn't invent any the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It's a short, well-organised memo that fits on one page, as the brief asked.
